item.title: Your Italian Pension as a Non-EU Professional: What You Build and When
item.description: How INPS contributions work for people who move to Italy mid-career, the 2026 retirement rules, the contribution ceiling, and what happens if you leave.

item.title: Leave in Italy and Long Trips Home: Planning Holidays as a Relocated Employee
item.description: Four weeks of statutory leave, extra hours under the CCNL, public holidays and the August slowdown: how relocated professionals can plan visits home.

item.title: Do You Need to Speak Italian to Work in Italy on a Blue Card?
item.description: No language test for the Blue Card, but Italian matters for offices, landlords and daily life. What to expect and how to get started.

item.title: Italy, Germany or the Netherlands? A Blue Card Comparison for Candidates
item.description: Salary thresholds, permanent residence, and employment rules in three EU Blue Card countries, from the point of view of a non-EU professional choosing where to go.

item.title: Losing Your Job on an Italian Blue Card: What Happens Next
item.description: Dismissal, resignation or the end of a contract: what you receive, how long you can stay, how to change employer, and what the Blue Card allows you to do.

item.title: Probation in Italy When You Move on a Work Visa
item.description: How the Italian probation period works, what it means for a relocated employee and their sponsor, and how to use it well on both sides.

item.title: Permanent or Fixed-Term Contract: What It Changes for Your Italian Permit
item.description: A permanent contract gives a two-year Blue Card; a fixed-term one gives the contract length plus three months. How contract type affects permit, renewal and planning.

item.title: Why Your Collective Agreement (CCNL) Matters for Your Permit
item.description: The CCNL sets the minimum salary for your level, your hours, leave and notice. For a sponsored employee it is also part of the salary test. What to check.

item.title: Your First Italian Payslip: How Gross Becomes Net
item.description: Employee social security, IRPEF bands, employment tax credits and local surcharges, explained for professionals who just moved to Italy.

item.title: Reading an Italian Offer: RAL, Installments and the Blue Card Threshold
item.description: Italian offers state the RAL, the annual gross salary. Why it is the figure that counts for the Blue Card, what is not included in it, and how to compare it with an offer from home.

item.title: Blue Card or Quota Permit? Choosing the Right Italian Work Visa in 2026
item.description: Italy has 43,300 non-seasonal quota places for 2026, but qualified professionals can skip the quota entirely. How to tell which route fits your profile.
